definitions.explanation: A more formal or literary expression for free time.
Used when taking one's leave, especially in formal situations.

examples.japanese: {数|かぞ}え{上|あ}げれば{暇|いとま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: There's no end to listing them all.

examples.japanese: ⟦{忙|いそが}しくて→忙しい：00591_isogashii⟧⟦{休|やす}む→休む：00606_yasumu⟧{暇|いとま}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: I'm so busy I don't even have time to rest.

examples.japanese: ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{枚挙|まいきょ}→枚挙：13153_maikyo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{暇|いとま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: The problems are too numerous to list.

examples.japanese: ⟦そろそろ→そろそろ：01259_sorosoro⟧お{暇|いとま}⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I should take my leave now.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長居|ながい}→長居：14517_nagai⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧しまいました。お{暇|いとま}⟦いたします→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
examples.english: I've overstayed. I shall take my leave.

examples.japanese: {暇|いとま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げて→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧⟦{帰路|きろ}→帰路：16079_kiro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ついた。
examples.english: I said my farewells and headed home.

notes:
{暇|いとま} is a formal/literary reading of the kanji ⟦{暇|ひま}→暇：00592_hima⟧. It appears primarily in set expressions rather than in casual conversation.

SENSE 1 — SPARE TIME:
Used in formal expressions about having (or lacking) time:
- {暇|いとま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: to have no time, to be endless
- ⟦{枚挙|まいきょ}→枚挙：13153_maikyo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{暇|いとま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: too numerous to count (set phrase)
- ⟦{休|やす}む→休む：00606_yasumu⟧{暇|いとま}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: not even time to rest

SENSE 2 — LEAVE-TAKING:
A formal way of excusing oneself:
- ⟦お{暇|いとま}する→お暇する：16267_oitomasuru⟧: to take one's leave (polite)
- {暇|いとま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧: to bid farewell (literary)
- お{暇|いとま}⟦いたします→いたす：01314_itasu⟧: I shall take my leave (very polite)

CONTRAST WITH ひま:
- ⟦{暇|ひま}→暇：00592_hima⟧: free time, not busy (everyday word)
- {暇|いとま}: spare time, leave-taking (formal/literary)

The same kanji is read differently: ひま is casual and common; いとま is elevated and restricted to set phrases.
